summary: Mitchell G. Weiss is an Indology scholar who studied under Ludo Rocher. He served as a professor at the University of Basel.
Mithilesh Chaturvedi works in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Delhi in the Department of Sanskrit (attested 2009) and as professor emeritus (attested 2026).

Mitsuji Fukunaga (1918–2001) specialized in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies, studying at Hiroshima Higher Normal School and Kyoto University. His academic career included posts at Kyoto University, the University of Tokyo, Kansai University, and the University of Kitakyushu.
Mitsukuni Yoshida (1921–1991) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1942–1945) and held a post at Kyoto University of the Arts (~1985–1991).
Mitsutoshi Moriguchi (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also served as a lecturer (attested 1989–1995).
Mitsuyo Demoto is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. Demoto held a post at the University of Marburg (attested 2024).

Mitsuyoshi Saegusa (1923–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at First Higher School, the University of Tokyo, the University of Munich, and Kokugakuin University, later holding professorships at the University of Tsukuba and Nihon University.

Mitsuyuki Ishida (1911–1991) specialized in Buddhist studies, studying at Ryukoku University (~1931–1934). He taught at Ryukoku University from ~1949 to 1976 and served as a professor at Shitennoji University (~1976–1982).
Miyako Notake is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She held part-time lecturer positions at Waseda University, attested in 2015 and 2026.
Miyoko Nakano (born 1933) is a Sinologist who studied at Hokkaido University (~1952–1956). She later served on the faculty at Hokkaido University from ~1971 to 1996.

Mizuho Okita (born 1977) specializes in Indology and religious studies, having studied at Tokai University and Gakushuin University under Katsuhiko Kamimura and Atsuhiko Yoshida. Okita served as a part-time lecturer at Meisei University (attested 2008).
Mizumaro Ishida (1917–2003) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who served as a professor at Tokai University (attested in 1976 and 1987).
Mohammad Ashraf Dar specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. Dar earned a Master of Philosophy at Vikram University and was attested there as a research scholar in 2014.
Mohammad Habib (1895–1971) was an Indology and history scholar who studied at the University of Allahabad, Aligarh Muslim University (~1912–1916), and New College (~1916–1920).

Mohan G. Dhadphale works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000) and editor of Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).

Mokurai Shimaji (1838–1911) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under Chō Sanshū. He served as Geschäftsführer at Nishi Hongan-ji (1870) and 25th head priest at Gankyo-ji (1892–1905).

Mona Schrempf specializes in Tibetology and religious studies, completing a doctorate in anthropology at the Free University of Berlin in 2001. In 2006, she was attested as a research fellow at Humboldt University of Berlin and a part-time teacher at Heidelberg University.

Monica Esposito (1962–2011) was a Sinology and religious studies scholar educated at Ca' Foscari, Fudan, Ghent, Shanghai Academy of Social Sciences, and Paris Diderot. She held postdoctoral positions at Venice, the Sorbonne, and Kansai University, becoming associate professor at Kyoto University in 2003.

Monica L. Smith specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology, having studied at the University of Michigan (~1990–1997). She held a post at the University of Pittsburgh (2000–2002) before joining the University of California, Los Angeles as a professor in 2002.

Monier Monier-Williams (1819–1899) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Balliol College and University College, Oxford, under Horace Hayman Wilson. He taught at East India Company College and Cheltenham College before serving as Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit (1860–1887).
